At most sixteen variables are allowed, and every head variable must occur in a premise. There are no function symbols, implicit negation, probabilistic truth claims or automatic relation types. query: Can a fact without sources or with an unknown source participate in inference?
reference_quote: Fact::new(id, statement).with_sources(...) supplies immutable caller facts. ReasoningOptions::new(revision, known_sources) supplies the explicitly registered source-ID set. A fact without sources or referencing an unknown source is excluded from deduction, counted in missing_support_count and listed up to 100 IDs in missing_support (possibly fewer after output budgeting). query: Ändert infer die Faktenbasis oder liefert es Vorschläge mit Beweisketten?
reference_quote: infer returns proposals, never updates the facts or a knowledge database. Each Proposal has its statement, rule ID and canonical rule fingerprint, typed immediate premise references (Fact ID or earlier Proposal ID), transitive base fact IDs and source IDs. Rule::body/head/to_json expose the exact rule; fingerprint identifies its canonical representation, not its authenticity. Preserve that representation with the application audit record. Only one deterministic proof is retained per new statement. Inputs/rules are sorted by ID; rounds use only already committed local proof nodes. Cycles can still imply self-relations under a caller's transitive rule; decide whether such a rule makes sense for your domain.

query: Does a contradiction choose a winning statement or make unrelated statements true?
reference_quote: Explicit positive/negative opposites appear as Conflict reference pairs, including conflicts involving a derived proposal. query: What default bounds limit reasoning rounds, join trials, proposals and serialized output?

query: How do a DatasetManager clone and a separately constructed manager differ?
reference_quote: `DatasetManager::new(namespace, config)` starts an empty generation zero with a random 128-bit identity. Revisions reuse the validated StoreRevision format: namespace, identity and generation in 0..=i64::MAX. Compare the **complete** value. A manager clone shares the same publication slot; a separately created manager gets another identity. The revision describes this in-process dataset lineage, not an implicit storage backend or an authentication capability.

query: Wann prüfen prepare und publish die erwartete Revision einer vorbereiteten Änderung?

Losing concurrent work returns Conflict without publishing any part. The old snapshot is released outside the write lock. Generation exhaustion fails without publication. Prepared data has private fields and cannot be deserialized or edited into an unchecked candidate.

query: What does an old reader see after a newer complete dataset snapshot is published?
reference_quote: Old readers deliberately retain the old complete snapshot while new readers acquire the new one. `require_current(view.revision())` checks whether a retained view is still current at that instant. It does not guarantee that no future publication occurs after the check. Capture the revision alongside results, preserve the Arc when original text or sources are needed later, and recheck freshness/access under application policy before sending externally. Calling snapshot separately for every component can mix different generations; reuse one acquired view.

query: Wann benötigt eine Änderung am Text eines semantischen Datensatzes einen EmbeddingProvider?
reference_quote: Select `DatasetConfig::with_embedding_space` to enable semantic mode. New or byte-changed text then requires a matching EmbeddingProvider. Vector dimensions, finite values, counts and model recipe are validated through the existing semantic API. No record with pending vectors is published. Exact unchanged text reuses its existing Arc-backed vector even when metadata or source bindings change; metadata is not part of the provider's text input. Deletes remove vectors. A wrong provider supplied for an update requiring inference fails; an unused provider is not invoked.

query: Does a metadata-only DatasetRecord update automatically preserve old source bindings?
reference_quote: Every Put **replaces** the entry's source bindings. DatasetRecord::new starts with no sources; omitting sources clears previous bindings, including for metadata-only puts. Supply a checked complete list when preserving them is intended. Nothing silently retains old citations after a text replacement. Missing references are allowed and remain Missing; the system does not invent evidence.

query: Welche Bestandteile des StoreRevision-Tokens müssen bei einer Revision verglichen werden?
reference_quote: Each `StoreRevision` contains a namespace, random 128-bit lowercase-hex identity and generation in 0..=i64::MAX. Compare the **complete** token. Every read/page/write receives the expected token and fails with `Conflict` if it differs. Nonempty accepted batches increment the generation once, including equal-value puts or deleting an absent ID. Empty batches check the token and leave the generation unchanged. Exhaustion fails without mutation. `renew_identity` keeps records, generates a new identity and resets generation to zero.

query: Is a StoreChange batch published partially when an entry or duplicate ID is invalid?
reference_quote: `StoreChange::Put` inserts/replaces an entire entry; `Delete` removes an ID. A batch is atomic: validate every entry, duplicate ID and budget before changing records; commit every operation plus its revision or return an error with no partial commit. Commit counts distinguish accepted puts from actual deletions. A custom adapter must uphold the same contract; AIRust cannot repair a dishonest adapter that mutates without advancing its token.

query: Wie funktionieren die exklusive after-Grenze und next_after beim seitenweisen Lesen?
reference_quote: `page(expected, after, limit)` returns strictly increasing UTF-8-byte-ordered IDs, exclusively after the supplied ID. It respects both row and encoded-record byte budgets. `next_after` equals the last returned ID only when more records exist. A record that does not fit the remaining page is deferred, never skipped. If one record cannot fit an empty page, return a limit error. A cursor is meaningful only with its namespace/revision; restarting at a newer revision is an explicit caller decision.

query: What entry, batch and page byte budgets does StorageLimits permit by default?
reference_quote: `StorageLimits::default()` permits 4,096-byte IDs, 1 MiB encoded entries, 1,000 operations / 16 MiB per batch, and 1,000 rows / 4 MiB per page. Metadata is capped at depth 64 and 100,000 JSON nodes. Builders validate positive limits; depth cannot exceed 64. Limits count UTF-8/encoded JSON bytes, including escapes, not characters or total heap. Put/delete IDs within a batch must be unique. Invalid IDs, blank text, malformed stored JSON and ID/record disagreement fail explicitly.

query: Was liefert read_snapshot, wenn sich während des seitenweisen Lesens die Revision ändert?

It validates ordering, cursors, entries and page budgets even for custom adapters. A concurrent write or malformed page discards the staged load; it returns no partially usable snapshot. The default snapshot permits 128 rows per page, one million entries and 128 MiB encoded records. Configure `SnapshotOptions` within the backend page limits; retry conflicts with bounded application policy rather than an endless internal loop.

query: Which journal mode, synchronous setting and default busy timeout does file-backed SQLite storage use?
reference_quote: File-backed writes use SQLite WAL and `synchronous=FULL`, immediate transactions, parameterized values and a default five-second busy timeout. Reads fence revision and rows in one read transaction. Set a bounded alternative with `set_busy_timeout`; a busy/SQL/commit error propagates and the transaction rolls back. Separate connections racing with the same token produce one successful writer and a conflict (or a lock timeout if the writer cannot acquire the lock). Read-only writes/identity renewal fail. `in_memory` follows the same data contract but reports non-durable storage.

query: Wie bleiben ursprüngliche UTF-8-Spannen bei Unicode-Normalisierung erhalten?
reference_quote: Normalization applies NFKC/lowercase processing while mapping normalized segments back to original graphemes. Analyzed terms are normalized again before optional stemming. Compatibility ligatures, combining marks and expansions keep safe original UTF-8 spans. Multiple expanded tokens can refer to the same original grapheme; offsets are not normalized-string offsets. A phrase span covers the first through last matching original token, including intervening punctuation/whitespace. It is an analyzed token phrase, not a byte-exact substring.

query: Does German Snowball split compounds or recognize irregular verbs such as gehen and ging?
reference_quote: German Snowball maps useful forms such as Haus/Häusern, Katze/Katzen and Führerschein/Führerscheine. It does not provide full lemmatization, compound splitting, synonym recognition or irregular-verb understanding: gehen and ging remain different. Stemming may conflate unrelated meanings, including schön/schon. It is fixed, explicit analysis, not a truth or semantic-relevance model. The selected implementation is `rust-stemmers` 1.2.0; do not assume every rule in later upstream Snowball revisions is included.

query: Welche Reihenfolge und Nachbarschaft müssen Wörter einer zitierten Phrase erfüllen?
reference_quote: `search(query, &TextSearchOptions)` accepts unquoted words and required double-quoted phrases. Every quoted phrase must match in its analyzed token order with no intervening token. Overlapping occurrences are supported. Punctuation and whitespace can separate adjacent tokens. No stop words are removed, so phrases do not silently bridge removed words. Stemming also applies inside phrases when enabled.

query: What happens when a phrase has an unclosed quote or contains no searchable tokens?

Empty phrases, phrases without searchable tokens and unclosed quotes return typed errors instead of bypassing phrase constraints. Empty/whitespace queries fail; punctuation-only unquoted queries can return no hits. This is not a Boolean/wildcard/regex/fuzzy query language.

query: Ist eine gelöschte Kennung mit Tombstone bei ExpectedRevision wieder Absent?
reference_quote: Every write requires `ExpectedRevision::Absent` for a never-seen ID or `Exact(current_revision)`. A deleted ID has a tombstone and is not absent. `upsert` inserts/replaces/recreates content, `delete` records a deletion, and `restore` copies an available prior or current state into a new revision. Restore can restore deletion and never rewinds the sequence. Invalid entries, stale expectations, missing/pruned revisions and sequence exhaustion return errors without changing current records, revision heads or history. Applications coordinate their own locks and database transactions.

query: Are ChangeMetadata actor and reason values authenticated identities?
reference_quote: `ChangeMetadata::default()` is empty. Optional checked actor/reason builders accept 1..1024 plain-text characters, trim surrounding spaces and reject controls. Arbitrary JSON metadata is optional. Labels are caller claims, not authenticated identities or a tamper-proof audit log. The engine invents no wall-clock time.

query: Wie viel Textgeschichte bewahrt VersionedIndex standardmäßig auf?
reference_quote: The default history limit is zero: revisions/conflicts work without retaining historical text. `with_history_limit(n)` opts into at most n committed snapshots globally, including deletion states and possibly current snapshots. Reducing the limit prunes immediately; increasing it does not recover previously unrecorded history. Snapshot text is copied only when this journal is enabled. The limit counts records, not bytes; choose it for actual text sizes. This is a bounded helper, not full event sourcing or permanent application history.

query: Which revision and tombstone consistency rules does versioned JSON validate?
reference_quote: Versioned JSON format 1 preserves current records, heads/tombstones, the sequence and retained journal. Imports validate entry IDs/text, unique heads, exact live/deleted agreement, positive/ordered revision identities, action/state consistency, current-snapshot agreement and journal capacity. `from_json` defaults to a 16 MiB input cap; `from_json_with_limit` sets a caller policy. Generic Serde validates the schema under the caller's input-resource policy. Numeric u64 revisions require consumers that preserve integer precision. Loading rebuilds the lexical index; portable `Engine` source JSON and derived cache format remain separate.

query: Was muss eine Anwendung nach dem Laden eines älteren vollständigen Index-Snapshots koordinieren?
reference_quote: Loading an older whole-index snapshot is an application-level rollback, not the `restore` operation. Start a new coordination epoch and discard outstanding expected revisions when performing such a rollback. This library cannot detect a caller replacing its entire authoritative snapshot with an older one.

query: Does pruning history also remove revision heads and deleted-ID tombstones?
reference_quote: History pruning does not remove revision heads or tombstones. Their memory cost follows all tracked IDs, including deleted ones. Reclaiming those identities requires an application-controlled new coordination epoch so old expected revisions cannot be reused.
